posts.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
posts.summary:
HBM shortages threaten AI expansion; TSMC weighs price hikes; advanced packaging ramps; domain-specialized AI models; Infineon and UMC boost fab investments; Intel's quantum move; Lam and imec advance 3D integration; Google expands TPUs; AI-driven earnings; CPU benchmarking methodology for agentic AI.
The post Chip Industry Week In Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Memory supply constraints for HBM and DRAM are projected to persist through 2029-2030, with major suppliers like SK hynix and Samsung reporting sold-out capacity for the coming years.
TSMC is considering a 20% price increase for CoWoS packaging services as AI-driven demand continues to outstrip available advanced-packaging capacity.

Foundry and manufacturing investments are accelerating, highlighted by Infineon’s €1.1B GaN power semiconductor facility and UMC’s $3.2B capital expenditure boost for advanced packaging and silicon photonics.
Intel reported improved manufacturing execution on its 18A process node and released its 14A 0.9 PDK, signaling progress in its efforts to attract external foundry customers.
China’s CXMT is attempting to enter the HBM3E market despite significant technical hurdles, currently reporting low manufacturing yields between 20% and 30%.

posts.title: Tesla launches new financing plan in China, halving minimum down payments
posts.summary:
Down payments for select Model 3 and Model Y variants fall to 39,900 yuan ($5,940), half the previous level.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Tesla has introduced aggressive financing incentives in China, halving minimum down payments to 39,900 yuan for select Model 3 and Model Y variants.
The promotion includes a 5-year zero-interest financing plan, aimed at stimulating demand following four consecutive months of year-on-year delivery declines in the region.
The incentive structure, which runs through November 30, utilizes a balloon payment model to lower monthly financial burdens for consumers.
This move highlights the intensifying price competition in the Chinese EV market as Tesla attempts to defend its market share against domestic rivals.

posts.title: Xiaomi follows Li Auto with planned Sunwoda EVB investment to deepen battery ties
posts.summary:
Xiaomi plans to invest about $253 million for a 5.34% stake in Sunwoda EVB, becoming its third-largest shareholder.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi is investing 1.7 billion yuan ($253 million) for a 5.34% stake in Sunwoda EVB, signaling a strategic move to secure its battery supply chain.
Sunwoda will lose control of its battery subsidiary following a board reshuffle and capital increase, leading to the deconsolidation of the unit from its financial statements.
The deconsolidation is expected to boost Sunwoda's 2026 net profit by 3.2 billion to 4.5 billion yuan due to the remeasurement of its remaining stake at fair value.
Sunwoda has officially terminated its plans for a Hong Kong IPO, citing shifting market conditions and internal strategic priorities.

posts.title: 2026.44: At Long Last…
posts.summary: The best Stratechery content from the week of October 26, 2026 including Anthropic numbers, the end of the Internet as we know it, and autocracies then and now.
bullets: Anthropic’s S-1 filing provides the first transparent look at the economics of a frontier AI lab, finally allowing for empirical analysis of their business model.
The current trajectory of AI development suggests an imminent rupture of the global internet as we know it, potentially forcing a shift toward more localized, private digital experiences.
Internal instability within the Chinese bureaucracy, driven by Xi Jinping’s aggressive anti-corruption crackdowns, suggests that the narrative of an inevitable 'Chinese century' may be overstated.

posts.title: The Download: GLP-1s and eating disorders, self-aware cities, and forever chemicals
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse. GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are one of the biggest biotech breakthroughs of the last decade. But to some clinicians, they can…
bullets: Binance has experienced the largest cryptocurrency hack in history, marking a significant security event for the digital asset sector.

Global incidence rates for anorexia and bulimia nervosa increased by 71% between 1990 and 2023, raising concerns about the intersection of mental health and the widespread adoption of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs.
Emerging remediation technologies are targeting the removal of PFAS 'forever chemicals' from water systems to mitigate long-term health risks like cancer and immune system suppression.
The intersection of biotech breakthroughs and public health trends suggests a complex regulatory and ethical landscape for pharmaceutical companies moving forward.
